steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Ow... my head hurts... This reset feels nothing like what happened in the murder mystery game. It's like I actually died...

It sounds extra convincing coming from someone who has literally set one foot into the coffin multiple times. Too bad the room is completely silent, with no one to respond to you. You rub your temples and sit up in the sterile white void. Reluctantly, you start reviewing what happened once again.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: She was right after all. This fragment of the script is completely beyond her control. She can't guide me or rewrite the story like she did in Cirrenfold. I'm afraid even the reset trigger here doesn't follow Irrheia's logic.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: If that's the case, it could explain why even though I deliberately followed Irrheia's suggestions and intentionally broke the usual patterns to show her different outcomes, I still got reset.
After everything you've experienced, you're no longer the blank slate you were when you first awoke. The Sinners have shown you many kinds of entertainment.

In video games and murder mystery games, an illusion is often the manifestation of its creator's obsession. To succeed, you must outperform the owner of the obsession. If Irrheia doesn't govern this place, but the Mania lingering in her consciousness does, it'll only make this principle more true.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But... how exactly do I meet the criteria for success here? If Irrheia herself isn't providing the clues... then perhaps what matters is her earliest desire, from before she was contaminated by Mania?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It can't be about escape. She's already accomplished that herself. What does "better" really mean in this context? Not earlier, not madder either...
Then...
Is "better" really what she needs?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Well... I don't have any better options anyway.
You don't let the fleeting insight slip away. Of course, it's just a hunch. You're far from certain. But at this point, you have no reason to hesitate. You'll test your theory boldly.

So you lie back down on the bed and dutifully play the role of an obedient "medical resource." You allow yourself to be nurtured to the perfect condition. Time stretches unbearably when you take no action of your own, but you wait patiently.

Day after day of exercise, medication, and examinations, interspersed with tutoring and reading time doled out as rewards. You become so cooperative that even your family is astounded, and even after learning you've been cast aside, you simply obey instructions and leave home to live independently.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: The figures didn't look so good last month! I know it's not easy to consistently produce high-quality content, and players grow bored quickly, but that's just how this mystery game business works. Your script gotta grab enough attention!

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: You know how these Eastsiders are these days. They're all empty inside and craving virtual thrills. That's how we make money! We gotta satisfy the customers, Irrheia. Put in the hard work and you'll push through it, right? I know you can do it!

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Just be more mindful next time, okay? Your previous work The Charming Snake's Dream was very popular, but that doesn't mean you can just follow it with The Silly Panda's Bamboo Wish! We pulled the first one exactly because people got tired of it, remember?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Got it, Boss.

On your way home from work, you receive a lengthy message from your boss. You mechanically react with a thumbs up and reply with a "Got it" before switching back to the email tab to finish your daily report. The single word "script-writing" summarizes your entire day. Write, delete, repeat.

This is the best job you could find. You work nine to five. You get the weekends off. You can make ends meet. You get meager bonuses. Your boss's favorite activities are counting profits and pressuring employees. No endless Corruptors to kill or Black Rings to absorb.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Wait, two more seconds until I can clock out... I won't make this light. Whatever. Got another hour to wait before I can buy the discounted sandwiches from the convenience store near my apartment.

Bustling crowds come and go around you, the same people passing you by at the same time every day. They hurry along with eyes fixed on their phones. Nobody so much as glances at you, an employee of a murder mystery game parlor commuting in a witch costume.

This is daily life in Eastside. When technology occupies everyone with cheap thrills, the dazzling spectacles eventually become dull. Overstimulation numbs the senses, leaving people desperately craving new identities, new lives, and new roles to play.

You're no different, except your witch costume changes nothing. Art imitates life, and your life consists of clocking in, working, then clocking out. Occasionally, you catch the news broadcast, and that has inspired you to write The Dancing Beauty of the Great Expo.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: DisCity Independence Day is next week and we need to cash in on that! Be prepared to work overtime. Please reply if you've seen this message.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: Let's take a vote on this year's team-building event. I personally recommend option 1. It's cheaper and just as effective.

steps.speaker: Boss
steps.content: We're adjusting the lunch subsidy policy. Only those scheduled for the day shift will be eligible. Off-duty employees and office support staff will no longer receive it. It'll start this month. Don't be alarmed when you get your paycheck.

It's as if you've really spent years within this story, until you've become just another featureless face. Even your witch costume doesn't make you stand out from the rush hour Eastside crowds. And you finally get the proof you've been waiting for.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: My dear Chief, what are you doing? Yes, nothing, just playing by the rules... Do you think this will impress me? Hah, no one wants to watch such a boring story. It's so repetitive and uncreative.

The voice suddenly rings out, as if someone is whispering in your ear, hair brushing past your ear before vanishing. She maintains that ethereal, smiling tone, but the fact that she's spoken first should be some kind of indication.
And this is exactly what you've been waiting for. You straighten your posture within the crowd, as if you've anticipated her "appearance" all along.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I don't find this boring. True, this is not an "interesting" life, but it's peaceful. If my Sinners could live like this, I'd be happy for them.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Oh? You seem quite content to waste your life away here. Fine then, I can certainly gift you this boring existence if that's what you want.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: But doesn't this mean you choose to lose the bet? What a shame. Have you finally realized you stand no chance of winning? It seems your unbridled creativity and unyielding pride have been worn away completely.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I do hope to retire early someday and live a stable life away from danger. But... I never said I planned to spend my whole life here. Indeed, I'm quitting.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Quitting? Are you begging for mercy now? Do you think I'll spare you just like that?
You keenly detect a hint of disappointment in her tone. For someone usually so inscrutable, this is already a rare display of emotion. It gives you more confidence to proceed with your plan.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Of course not. I remember you said you couldn't control this place, and I'm not giving up yet. I'm attempting to stay in the game by saying "I quit" to the version of you that controls this place.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: ...Has the boring life worn away your sanity as well?

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I'm simply trying to guess what you truly want. At first, I realized you weren't lying. After gaining your power, you saw through the Ashworth family's hypocrisy and arrogance. You recognized how they deceived and exploited you.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But someone who has truly broken free wouldn't voluntarily return here time after time. The very existence of this script is itself a clue pointing toward the answer. On the surface, it appears I'm trapped here, dying repeatedly, while you can quit whenever you please...

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But in reality, the one dying has always been "Irrheia," your past self. Each of our attempts, which are really your attempts, to find a "better outcome," is the prison itself.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I understand you. Every time I escape a plight, I too can't help but wonder: Why couldn't I see through it earlier? I could have done better. But this refusal to accept what happened also traps us in the past.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: All these pretty words, but you're just rearranging the connections between facts. The result is still the same. If you truly understand as you claim, then you shouldn't want to quit. You should keep trying, shouldn't you?
You swivel your chair and look up, searching for Irrheia's position in the air above you. You know you can't actually make eye contact with her, but you want her to feel the weight of your sincerity.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No. I won't keep trying, because I already know what you want. I also know that if everything presented in this script is true, then there could never be a so-called "better" ending.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: No one could have done better than you did in those circumstances, Irrheia. You endured such a past. You were deceived, brainwashed, exploited, and ultimately discarded. Yet you broke free from those chains entirely on your own, still existing as yourself independently.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I've tried, and so have many other Sinners. Even with our ability to cheat, to reset, and retry with memories from the previous rounds, we still couldn't do better than you. No one in the world could. You should have been freed from here long ago. You deserve it.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Is flattering me your new strategy? Then you're likely to be disappointed. Save your sugar-coated bullets. This alone won't be enough to sway me. Keep trying the wrong approach, and you might really remain trapped here forever.
You're unfazed by this half-hearted threat.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: This isn't flattery. It's simply the truth. If I've truly misread the situation, and you've long gotten over this, then let me pay the price for my presumption. But I'm not saying all this just to get myself out of here.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I don't want you to remain trapped in this impossible what-if scenario, tormenting both yourself and others. Irrheia, you never did anything wrong as a child. She was already so brave. Please stop denying her and killing her, will you?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: The one who killed her... was never... me...

Irrheia is still in denial, but her voice draws out and breaks off unnaturally, finally vanishing into the spatial fissure, as if she's restraining something. Soon after, she vanishes completely once more, resuming her role as a mere spectator.

Yet you know that even in Irrheia's absence, the part of her long trapped in the past remains. It's the very thing she's been struggling to suppress. The fracturing space before you confirms everything, as the room rapidly collapses.

The illusion begins to unravel, and you're thrown into a weightless vortex, the world spinning violently. Instinctively, you try to close your eyes to steady yourself, but you force them open again. In the shattered mirror fragments, you glimpse what appears to be young Irrheia's face.

steps.speaker: Young Irrheia
steps.content: Is that true? Are there really no "better" and "smarter" choices than the ones I made?

Her childish face is etched with exhaustion. Her gaze is both vacant and defiant, as if she's shouldering a burden that should never have been hers. She stares right into your eyes, her lips barely moving, like it's taking all her courage to force out the words.

You've experienced many failures yourself. You know what will help her break free isn't some hypothetically perfect alternative, but rather an affirmation. That at least under those specific circumstances, she already did her best.
In that moment, she freezes, her tense expression finally relaxes, and her lips curve into a smile. A smile of long-awaited relief and peace.

The fissures collapse all at once, mirror shards raining down around you. The hospital ward, the sanatorium, and the room all vanish completely. You're thrown out of the illusion, a sudden release of pressure in your chest as you awaken in your own body in the real world.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: How does it feel to return safely to reality? Pleasant, I imagine. After all, you got everything you wanted, and claimed your victory. Now you understand me better than I understand myself.

Your vision gradually comes into focus as the wavering shapes before your eyes solidify into Irrheia's perfectly composed form. She still rests her chin lightly on her hand, a smile playing at her lips, as if she has no objection to your actions in her script, or is even appreciative of them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: There's an old saying in Eastia: "Those in the midst of a situation often see less clearly than bystanders." And another: "A single leaf before your eyes can hide an entire mountain." Some problems simply cannot be seen from where you already stand. That was true for you, and true for your childhood self as well.
This is why you're always extraordinarily patient with Sinners. Because you know that sometimes they simply need someone to help them see clearly.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: You don't see danger in me, but "problems"? What about my vengeance against my "family"? My uncontrollable power and my attitude?

options: Those are also just some of your problems.

choices.text: Those are also just some of your problems.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I never said I was interrogating you for your crimes. This interrogation is indeed part of the follow-up investigation into the Witchwoven Folio incident, but you're not the one who appears as a potential perpetrator.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: You may remember I mentioned that some customers were indeed negatively affected by your murder mystery games. But our in-depth investigation revealed that they already had criminal tendencies, and most had secretly acted on them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: The Public Security Bureau discovered this pattern. When they added the Ashworths to the list of suspected victims, they simultaneously placed them on the list of potential perpetrators. And you are very likely a victim of that family's abuse.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Me, a victim? The S-Class Sinner, the culprit who triggered a chain of incidents on a whim?
She seems amused by your words, her lips curving up mockingly. Her smile reveals both piqued interest and teasing disbelief toward your claims.
You don't react to her teasing. Instead, you pull out a note from the back of your folder and push it toward her. The note contains signatures from many different Sinners.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Yes, I am talking about you, and all these Sinners would agree too. Every one of them has spoken in your favor, even though you erased much of the information in that script you could still control.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: And after experiencing it personally, I found that they were absolutely right. Only by being in that position could I understand how difficult it was to break free on my own, and how difficult it was to maintain restraint once I had power.
You pull out another stack of documents filled with data and charts. The impassive printed text sits above a collection of distinct signatures.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Perhaps you never intended vengeance, much less to do good, but you did save children like yourself. The freely available technology and the charity foundation have made treatment more accessible and reduced the practice of breeding donor children.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Just like how your thrill-seeking activities ultimately gave lost and bored city-dwellers a sense of belonging, while exposing those who had already strayed from the right path.
Your sincere words don't seem to affect Irrheia at all. She regards you with mockery, like she's watching a child who has just proudly proclaimed their belief that kindness is human nature.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: So, you're saying that I'm a good person, huh? You've almost convinced me. So what's the Bureau's policy toward a kind soul like me? Surely you won't keep me detained here any longer?

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Since you've confirmed I haven't done anything evil and that I pose little danger, shouldn't you just let me go now?
Hearing that, a gleam flashes past your eyes as you realize you've caught the crux of the matter.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: But the MBCC's condition for releasing a Sinner is for them to be implanted with the shackles, to keep them under my supervision. As long as you meet this condition, you're certainly free to leave.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: So, will you allow me to give you the shackles?
The smile on Irrheia's lips widens, as though she's been waiting for these exact words.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: My dear Chief, you seem quite confident in your powers. Well, I don't mind a little conceit.

steps.speaker: Irrheia
steps.content: Very well. Then let me see just how much of my power these famous shackles of yours can actually restrain. I only hope... you won't regret this.
She extends her hand toward you invitingly, like an immortal witch awaiting a kiss on her hand. You round the desk and approach her, reaching out your hand as you gather your power.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: More than the supervisory function, I've always valued the perceptive power of the shackles more. I certainly have faith in them and won't regret this. After all, once the shackles are "truly" implanted, I can guarantee you full freedom.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Both inside and outside the illusion... so long as you release me from this illusion as well.
The previously composed Irrheia suddenly jerks her head up, instinctively trying to withdraw her hand! But it's too late. You immediately seize her wrist and activate your power!

Crimson thorns burst out, each one piercing into Irrheia's fair skin, like the blood drawn from her countless times in childhood, splattered all over her body, like a grotesque, bloodthirsty tree sprouting wildly from her flesh!

The root-like thorns pierce into the very core of everything, shattering the space around you! You watch as the woman's skin, long hair, and clothing dissolve into pale golden sand, flowing ceaselessly into an enormous hourglass at the foundation of this space!

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: <color=#dg1f1f>If you won't give me freedom, then I'll have to seize it myself.</color>
